title: Tracing an interbank transfer through the ledger
name: Ledger transfer tracing

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code creates, propagates, or finishes trace spans? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: In LedgerClient.post, span.end() is only called on the !res.ok path and the success path. If fetch itself rejects (the AbortSignal timeout fires, DNS fails, connection reset) or res.json() throws, the exception escapes the callback with the ledger.post_journal span never ended and never marked as an error. That span is never exported, so exactly the failures you most want to see (timeouts to the ledger) show up as a parent transfer.execute span with an error and a missing child. The fix is a try/catch/finally around the body that records the exception, sets ERROR status and always calls span.end().

choiceQuestions.prompt: Which span is the parent of ledger.post_journal, and what span ID does the ledger service receive in its traceparent header?
choices: transfer.reserve_funds is the parent; the ledger sees transfer.reserve_funds's ID
transfer.execute is the parent; the ledger sees transfer.execute's ID
There is no parent; the ledger receives a new root trace
transfer.execute is the parent; the ledger sees ledger.post_journal's ID
choiceQuestions.explanation: reserve_funds has already ended and its active context was restored when its callback returned, so when ledger.post is called the active span is transfer.execute. startActiveSpan makes ledger.post_journal active inside its callback, so propagation.inject(context.active(), ...) writes ledger.post_journal's span ID, making the ledger's server span its child. It is not a new root, and the parent's ID is not what gets injected.

choiceQuestions.prompt: store.reserve throws because the account has insufficient funds. Which spans end up with ERROR status?
choices: Neither, because the error is rethrown before status is set
choiceQuestions.explanation: The reserve_funds callback only has a finally that ends the child; it does not set status, so the child ends with UNSET status. The error propagates to execute's outer catch, which calls recordException and setStatus(ERROR) before rethrowing, and finally ends that span. So only transfer.execute is marked as an error.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why is the amount passed to the ledger as amountMinor.toString() rather than as the bigint itself?
choices: JSON.stringify throws a TypeError on bigint values, so it must be converted
The ledger API requires amounts in major units
Converting avoids floating-point rounding when the span attribute is recorded
toString() strips the currency so the ledger can apply its own
choiceQuestions.explanation: JSON.stringify cannot serialise a bigint and throws a TypeError, so the code converts it to a decimal string, which also preserves exact minor-unit precision. The value is still in minor units, it is not recorded as a span attribute, and a bigint carries no currency.
